items.text: Oil prices held relatively flat (WTI -0.1%, Brent +0.9% week-over-week), hovering around $90/bbl amid balanced supply/demand signals. For credit investors, persistent oil prices reduce energy sector stress but keep input costs sticky for manufacturing—a drag on corporate margins in an already-tightening yield environment.

Claims rose to 200k from 191k (w/o 11/7), signaling a modest uptick in layoff risk, while unemployment remains stable at 4.1%. Payroll growth moderated sharply to +165k in October from +60k prior. Early-stage deterioration in labor dynamics is now material for special-situations investors—expect increased default probability across leveraged names and cyclical credit.

Headline CPI at 3.72% YoY (Sep, latest), core at 2.57%, while PPI jumped to 6.52% YoY in Oct. The curve between headline and producer inflation signals supply-chain normalization is slowing. Sticky goods inflation and elevated input costs remain a headwind for already-stressed borrowers with limited pricing power.

Fed funds unchanged at 4.0%, with the 10Y UST climbing 12bps to 5.1% and the curve steepening 3bps to 27bps. Market pricing now shows ~94% probability of an ECB hike to 2.75% in Dec, suggesting divergence ahead: Fed on pause, ECB tightening. Rate vol and cross-curve dislocations create refinancing risk and spread widening pressure for duration-heavy credits.

HY OAS widened +23bps to 343, IG +3bps to 92, CCC +15bps to 1329, alongside a 605bps VIX spike to 25.46—highest in weeks. This marks a meaningful risk-off repricing; special-situations investors should monitor for idiosyncratic forced selling and covenant pressure, especially among vulnerable small- and mid-cap issuers.

Real retail sales (ex-autos, ex-gas, inflation-adjusted) edged down in October; core retail control group held at +0.6% m/m but off a weakening trend. GDP nowcast fell from 3.27% to 3.21%, and housing starts—while up 10% m/m—remain volatile. Growth is moderating into year-end; watch for credit deterioration among consumer-dependent and mortgage-sensitive names.

Consumer sentiment rebounded sharply in November preliminary to 51.0 from 48.0, but survey ended pre-election; cost-of-living anxiety remains highest since May (57% mention erosion). Existing home sales fell 5.5% to 3.75M SAAR, mortgage rates at 7.11%, signaling continued housing affordability stress. Longer-term consumer weakness and rising distress risk in residential-linked credit.

themeCards.title: Elevated refinancing wall 2027–28
themeCards.statusLine: HY OAS +23bps to 343, with yields now above 8%; ample issuance coming in Q1 and beyond. Mid-market leveraged credits face sharply higher roll costs as market re-prices risk.
themeCards.relevance: Refinancing risk is the highest single catalyst for special-situations opportunities; expect selective defaults, restructurings, and forced dividend cuts among names locked out or facing punitive pricing. Focus on Q1 2027 maturity cliffs and weak covenants.

themeCards.title: China economic deterioration & default risk
themeCards.statusLine: Official PMI fell to 49.3 (Oct), signaling manufacturing contraction; high-yield spreads widening amid property sector weakness. Policy stimulus has underdelivered; growth outlook is weakening.
themeCards.relevance: For credit investors with China exposure (direct or via supply-chain partners), rising sovereign and corporate default risk is material. Expect pressure on commodity exporters, logistics names, and anything financing China growth; structured credit and CDS opportunities may emerge.

themeCards.title: US labor-market inflection
themeCards.statusLine: Claims +9k WoW to 200k, payroll growth slowed to +165k in Oct; unemployment at 4.1% but trajectories are softening. Early signs of labor-market loosening.
themeCards.relevance: If jobless claims sustain 200k+ and payrolls fall further, credit stress will follow 3–6 months later. Watch for covenant pressure on leverage and interest-coverage multiples; elevated unemployment will increase default probability across all consumer-facing and cyclical sectors.

themeCards.title: Sticky goods inflation + credit margin squeeze
themeCards.statusLine: Headline CPI +3.72% YoY (Sep), PPI +6.52% (Oct); supply-chain pass-through still elevated. Services inflation persistent at 3.65–3.12% core PCE.
themeCards.relevance: Credit names with low pricing power (retail, restaurant, transportation, logistics) face margin compression as wage and input costs remain sticky. Monitor EBITDA trends closely; LBOs and highly leveraged credit are most vulnerable to margin surprises.

themeCards.title: Cross-curve inversion & rate volatility
themeCards.statusLine: 10Y-2Y curve steepened to 27bps; Fed on hold, ECB likely hiking Dec 17. VIX spiked to 25.46, highest in weeks. Yield curve dislocations and policy divergence creating volatility.
themeCards.relevance: Rate volatility and bear-steepening create duration losses on floating-rate paper; mark-to-market pain for asset-backed securities and hybrid paper. Expect maturities and covenant tests to tighten; refinancing windows narrow for weaker credits.

themeCards.title: Consumer discretionary stress & housing affordability crisis
themeCards.statusLine: Mortgage rates at 7.11%, existing home sales down 5.5% m/m; consumer sentiment weak (51.0 prelim, still -10% YTD) with 57% citing cost-of-living erosion. Retail sales momentum slowing.
themeCards.relevance: Housing-linked credits (MBS proxies, home builders, furniture, appliance) face significant stress. Consumer discretionary defaults will accelerate; expect opportunities in distressed consumer-credit issuers, auto ABS, and credit-card securitizations as affordability deteriorates.

regime.label: Mid-cycle slowdown
regime.detail: Fed on hold, curve steepening, labor cooling, credit spreads widening, sticky inflation, consumer stress rising.
